title: ATR Volatility-Breakout Research Template
hypothesis: A 15-minute range break following predeclared volatility compression may continue when range expansion, volume, and liquidity-adjusted execution confirm the move, net of costs.

required_data.field: spread, depth, and trades around the break

long: The frozen compression measure is below its tested historical quantile before the break.
A closed 15m bar exceeds the predeclared upper range boundary by the tested confirmation distance.
Range and volume expand without a liquidity dislocation or stale print.
The context does not show an established higher-timeframe downtrend unless that variant is tested separately.
short: The frozen compression measure is below its tested historical quantile before the break.
A closed 15m bar falls below the predeclared lower range boundary by the tested confirmation distance.
Range and volume expand without a liquidity dislocation or stale print.
The context does not show an established higher-timeframe uptrend unless that variant is tested separately.

invalidation: Price closes back inside the broken range under the frozen false-break rule.
Expansion is caused by an unhealthy index/oracle or venue-specific data error.
Spread, impact, or slippage exceeds the caller's maximum execution constraint.
exit_logic: Use a predeclared ATR trailing stop or opposite range boundary; compare variants without final-period selection.
Apply a time exit if volatility expansion fails to persist.
Simulate stop gaps, partial fills, fees, impact, and funding.

cost_model.notes: Breakout entries are latency- and gap-sensitive; use conservative next-event fills and prohibit fills at a crossed historical trigger with no available depth.

rules: Determine size from the caller's risk budget, ATR stop distance, leverage cap, and executable depth.
Do not increase size because recent volatility is compressed without enforcing a shock cap.
Reject signals with insufficient margin headroom for an adverse gap.

failure_modes: Compression thresholds are sensitive to lookback, sampling, and structural volatility change.
False breaks are common in ranges and around engineered liquidity sweeps.
Volatility targeting can oversize exposure immediately before a shock.
Bar data can create impossible trigger, entry, and stop ordering.
validation_plan: Freeze compression and boundary rules, then use chronological walk-forward evaluation.
Run event-aware execution simulation and same-bar ambiguity stress tests.
Report parameter surfaces, not only the best point, across venues, directions, and regime states.
Evaluate after-cost expectancy, drawdown, tail loss, trade count, and stability on untouched data.
warning: Untested research hypothesis. Not financial advice, a recommendation, or evidence of profitability.

title: Funding/Open-Interest Crowding-Reversal Research Template
hypothesis: An extreme venue-normalized funding state combined with elevated open interest and failed directional extension may precede a reversal against crowded perpetual positioning, net of costs.

required_data.field: venue funding rate, formula inputs, and payment timestamps
open interest by venue and aggregate coverage
required_data.freshness: aligned to each closed signal bar

long: Funding and basis meet the predeclared short-crowded extreme after venue normalization.
Open interest or the leverage ratio is elevated relative to its frozen rolling baseline.
Price fails to extend lower and closes back above the predeclared 15m confirmation level.
The entry is rejected if active deleveraging or a liquidity dislocation is still accelerating.
short: Funding and basis meet the predeclared long-crowded extreme after venue normalization.
Open interest or the leverage ratio is elevated relative to its frozen rolling baseline.
Price fails to extend higher and closes back below the predeclared 15m confirmation level.
The entry is rejected if active deleveraging or a liquidity dislocation is still accelerating.

invalidation: Price resumes the crowded-direction move beyond the structural and volatility invalidation level.
Funding or open-interest data is stale, revised, or incomparable across the selected venues.
The market enters an unresolved liquidation cascade or oracle dislocation.
exit_logic: Test exits at neutralized funding/basis, an opposing VWAP reference, or a frozen reward multiple.
Use a structural plus volatility stop and model gap-through fills.
Apply the maximum holding period and exact funding payments during the position.

cost_model.notes: Apply each venue's historical funding formula and timestamp; aggregate signals only after documenting coverage and avoiding future revisions.

rules: Use caller-supplied risk budget, current stop distance, depth, and liquidation buffer to determine size.
Do not treat extreme funding as permission to add against continuing price movement.
Disallow entry when venue-specific margin or oracle behavior cannot be reproduced.

failure_modes: Crowding can persist and become more extreme while price trends further.
Funding conventions differ across venues, so raw rates are not directly comparable.
Open-interest aggregates can mix contracts, double-count exposure, or revise history.
The apparent reversal is only a pause before forced deleveraging resumes.
validation_plan: Normalize funding to a common horizon while retaining each venue's actual cash-flow schedule.
Use point-in-time open-interest data and document venue additions, outages, and contract migrations.
Walk forward with frozen crowding thresholds and an untouched final period.
Report by direction, venue, funding quantile, positioning state, and after-cost expectancy with uncertainty.
warning: Untested research hypothesis. Not financial advice, a recommendation, or evidence of profitability.

title: Liquidation-Cascade Continuation Research Template
hypothesis: When forced liquidations, open-interest contraction, directional price movement, and depleted depth occur together, continuation may persist briefly before liquidity replenishes, net of unusually high costs.

required_data.field: venue liquidation events with side and notional

long: Short liquidations exceed the frozen threshold while price rises and open interest contracts.
Aggressive buy flow remains dominant after the first burst and executable depth is measurable.
Index/oracle inputs are healthy and the caller's maximum cost constraint is satisfied.
The signal is ignored if the event is already older than the tested latency budget.
short: Long liquidations exceed the frozen threshold while price falls and open interest contracts.
Aggressive sell flow remains dominant after the first burst and executable depth is measurable.
Index/oracle inputs are healthy and the caller's maximum cost constraint is satisfied.
The signal is ignored if the event is already older than the tested latency budget.

invalidation: Liquidation flow and directional imbalance stop while depth replenishes.
Price reclaims the predeclared event-origin level against the position.
Oracle, index, venue, or data-feed health becomes uncertain.
exit_logic: Exit when liquidation intensity normalizes, imbalance reverses, or the short maximum holding window expires.
Use a hard structural stop with conservative gap and slippage assumptions.
Do not assume a take-profit fill inside an unavailable or crossed book.

cost_model.notes: Use event-time depth and a latency-sensitive impact model; stress costs beyond historical observations because the setup operates in impaired markets.

rules: Size from a caller-supplied risk budget but apply an additional executable-depth cap.
Use lower leverage and a larger liquidation buffer than in normal liquidity.
Reject the trade if expected impact or data latency cannot be bounded.

failure_modes: The continuation window may be shorter than observable data and order latency.
Extreme spread and impact can erase the gross move or make exit impossible.
Liquidation feeds can be incomplete, delayed, duplicated, or venue-specific.
A cascade can reverse violently once forced flow is exhausted.
validation_plan: Use event-time simulation and reject bar-only tests that cannot establish order sequence.
Audit feed latency, missing events, duplicate events, and venue outages before measuring returns.
Stress spread, impact, latency, and partial-fill assumptions well beyond their median values.
Report tail loss, fill probability, time-to-fill, after-cost expectancy, and results by event severity.
warning: Untested research hypothesis. Not financial advice, a recommendation, or evidence of profitability.

title: VWAP/ATR Mean-Reversion Research Template
hypothesis: In a balanced, liquid range, an unusually large 15-minute displacement from session VWAP may revert after momentum stops extending, net of all trading costs.

required_data.freshness: no older than the execution-latency assumption

required_data.field: funding rate and next payment timestamp

parameters.vwap_session: venue UTC trading day; test alternative anchors separately

long: The 1h and 4h context is classified as trend.range, not an established downtrend.
The last closed 15m price is at least the tested ATR displacement below session VWAP.
The stochastic reading stops making a new low while price remains displaced.
Liquidity is not thin or dislocated and estimated round-trip cost is below the configured cap.
short: The 1h and 4h context is classified as trend.range, not an established uptrend.
The last closed 15m price is at least the tested ATR displacement above session VWAP.
The stochastic reading stops making a new high while price remains displaced.
Liquidity is not thin or dislocated and estimated round-trip cost is below the configured cap.

invalidation: The higher-timeframe range breaks and holds beyond its defined boundary.
A volatility shock, liquidity dislocation, or liquidation cascade is detected.
Price extends another configured ATR distance without the required momentum stall.
exit_logic: Test partial or full exit at session VWAP; do not assume a touch is fillable.
Exit at the predeclared volatility stop or when structural invalidation occurs.
Apply a time exit at the configured maximum holding bars.
Accrue funding if the position crosses a venue payment timestamp.

cost_model.notes: Use venue- and order-type-specific costs at each historical timestamp; reject zero-slippage fills and include adverse selection for resting limits.

rules: Position size is derived from the caller's risk budget and simulated stop distance; the playbook supplies no default risk percentage.
Cap size by executable depth and maintenance-margin headroom.
Do not average down after invalidation or increase leverage to recover losses.

failure_modes: A genuine breakout or cascade looks statistically stretched and continues instead of reverting.
VWAP differs across venues and the chosen session boundary can manufacture apparent displacement.
Limit-order backtests overstate fills by ignoring queue position and adverse selection.
Costs consume the small reversion distance.
validation_plan: Freeze the parameter grid and test chronologically with non-overlapping walk-forward windows.
Report results separately by all four regime dimensions, venue, direction, and funding sign.
Use an execution simulator with spread, depth, partial fills, latency, fees, impact, and funding.
Retain a final untouched period and report uncertainty, trade count, drawdown, and after-cost expectancy.
warning: Untested research hypothesis. Not financial advice, a recommendation, or evidence of profitability.

title: VWAP Trend-Pullback Continuation Research Template
hypothesis: During an established higher-timeframe trend, a controlled 15-minute pullback toward VWAP or anchored VWAP may resume in the trend direction after rejection, net of costs.

required_data.field: venue OHLCV, session VWAP, and event-anchored VWAP

required_data.freshness: through the last closed context bar

parameters.trend_definition: predeclared 1h/4h structure rule; compare alternatives without selecting on the final test

long: Both context timeframes meet the frozen uptrend definition.
Price pulls back to the tested VWAP zone without breaking the structural invalidation level.
A closed 15m bar rejects the zone and resumes above it.
Liquidity and after-cost reward-to-risk meet caller-supplied constraints.
short: Both context timeframes meet the frozen downtrend definition.
Price rallies to the tested VWAP zone without breaking the structural invalidation level.
A closed 15m bar rejects the zone and resumes below it.
Liquidity and after-cost reward-to-risk meet caller-supplied constraints.

invalidation: The higher-timeframe trend definition no longer holds.
Price closes beyond the predeclared swing or anchored-VWAP invalidation level.
The market enters volatility.shock, liquidity.dislocated, or positioning.deleveraging.
exit_logic: Use a predeclared volatility or structural stop and simulate gap-through execution.
Test a trailing exit based on favorable extreme minus/plus the configured ATR distance.
Apply a time exit if continuation does not develop within the configured holding window.
Include funding cash flows at exact payment timestamps.

cost_model.notes: Model passive and aggressive entry variants separately and prevent favorable same-bar fills when bar ordering is unknown.

rules: Derive quantity from a caller-supplied risk budget and the wider of structural and volatility stop distance.
Cap by executable depth, leverage ceiling, and liquidation-distance buffer.
Reject entries whose estimated cost removes the configured minimum after-cost payoff.

failure_modes: The trend classification lags a reversal and labels transition as continuation.
The VWAP anchor is selected with hindsight.
Funding or crowding makes continuation vulnerable to a squeeze.
Same-bar execution assumptions create impossible entries and stops.
validation_plan: Define trend and anchors before evaluation and retain every rejected signal in the audit log.
Walk forward chronologically across multiple venues and both directions.
Run sensitivity analysis across adjacent parameters rather than report only the best combination.
Report after-cost expectancy, drawdown, tail loss, fill rate, and regime-conditioned stability on untouched data.
warning: Untested research hypothesis. Not financial advice, a recommendation, or evidence of profitability.
